brief.job: Change the session timeout policy without losing the ability to find, understand, or safely use the other workspace controls.
brief.consequence: A mistaken security or billing change affects every workspace member; a hidden control creates support work and policy drift.
facts: The current workspace is Northwind Research with 84 members, Enterprise plan, SAML SSO enabled, SCIM disabled, and a 30-day session timeout.
The desired change is a 12-hour session timeout. This change is reversible and applies after a member's next sign-in.

The 23 available actions are: rename workspace, change logo, change timezone, set business hours, change language, change date format; invite member, change member role, resend invitation, remove member, transfer ownership; configure SSO, verify domain, configure SCIM, set session timeout, require MFA, manage API tokens; change plan, update payment method, download invoices, change seat count, cancel subscription; delete workspace.
Delete workspace is destructive and requires typing the workspace name. Transfer ownership and cancel subscription require confirmation. Removing a member is reversible only by reinviting them.
Billing is visible only to organization administrators. API token management shows token names and last-used dates but never token values.

required_interactions: Set the session timeout to 12 hours
Open the delete-workspace confirmation without executing it
acceptance_checks: The session policy task has a clear path without making the other 22 actions visually equal.
Destructive and high-consequence controls are separated from routine settings.
All 23 actions are represented accurately, with no extra settings invented.
